home-remodeling.local_heading: Remodeling behind the Harbor Islands gate
intro_paragraphs: Harbor Islands is not an old neighborhood, and that is the whole point. The eight enclaves behind the Harbor Island Drive gate, from The Estates and Harborview to Commodore Estates, Admiral's Cove and Grand Harbor Estates, went up from the late 1990s onward across roughly 192 acres of Hollywood waterfront. Most houses here are reaching their first serious remodel rather than their fourth. The wish lists repeat themselves: open the kitchen toward the Intracoastal, retire the formal living room nobody sits in, and swap a builder's idea of luxury for finishes you actually chose.

Your permit is issued by the City of Hollywood Development Services Department, where the Building Division reviews the plans. Broward adds a layer above the city: the county Board of Rules and Appeals administers the Florida Building Code countywide, publishes the local amendments, certifies the officials who review your drawings, and issues the Uniform Building Permit Application every Broward city uses. Broward also sits in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every replacement window and door needs HVHZ product approval. Then there is the association: exterior changes go to the Harbor Islands Property Owners Association for architectural review, and crews are registered at the guard gate before anyone swings a hammer.

The company behind that promise is licensed, insured and 20-plus years into South Florida work, with more than 150 remodels and additions delivered and inspected. In a community with 24-hour security, narrow streets and neighbors close enough to hear a saw, that record matters less than conduct: staged deliveries, clean sites at day's end, crews who know the gate procedure by name. You get a fixed written scope before demolition, a supervisor on site daily, protected floors and stair rails, and one accountable team from the first walk-through to the final inspection and the warranty behind it.

faqs.q: Who issues the permit for a remodel in Harbor Islands?
faqs.a: The City of Hollywood does, through its Development Services Department, on the Broward County Uniform Building Permit Application that every city in the county uses. The Board of Rules and Appeals sets how the Florida Building Code is administered across Broward and certifies the inspectors who show up. The association is separate and comes first for anything visible from outside, so we sequence architectural review ahead of plan review.

faqs.q: My house is from 1999. Is a full gut really necessary?
faqs.a: Usually not, and we will say so. Homes of this era have documented structure, hurricane provisions already in the design, and drawings on file, which means we can be surgical instead of destructive. What genuinely ages out is finishes, mechanical equipment, water heaters and the closed floor plan. We scope room by room, keep what is sound, and spend the budget where it changes how the house lives.

faqs.q: What is a realistic timeline for a full-house remodel?
faqs.a: Design and engineering usually run a couple of months, city review and association approval add more, and construction on a full house commonly runs several months to a year depending on scope. Impact glass and custom cabinetry are the long-lead items and get ordered first. You receive a written schedule with the estimate, and a supervisor whose job is to defend it.

faqs.q: Do most owners move out during construction?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Two-story layouts here often allow a phased approach where the upstairs stays livable while the ground floor is opened up, with dust barriers and a protected path to the door. Once ceilings are open and there is no kitchen, most owners relocate for the heavy phase. We decide that honestly at the walk-through, not halfway through demolition.

faqs.q: What does a remodel at this level cost in Harbor Islands?
faqs.a: There is no single number, and anyone who gives you one before seeing the house is guessing. Scope, selections and how much of the mechanical and glazing package you replace drive it far more than square footage. We price a written specification with real allowances, then hold it. PGX is a high-end builder, rarely the lowest of three bids, and clients hire us for the certainty.

kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Kitchen remodeling in Harbor Islands, Hollywood FL. The builder peninsula comes out and a real island goes in. Call PGX at (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: A kitchen for the water view

kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: When the builder kitchen runs out of road
intro_paragraphs: Walk into most Harbor Islands houses and the kitchen tells you the year. Bulkhead soffits above the wall cabinets, a corner pantry, a peninsula standing between the cook and everyone else, granite in a busy pattern, and cherry doors darker than the floor. On Windjammer Way and Harbor Court the room is often looking straight at the Intracoastal and doing nothing with it. So the kitchen remodeling brief here is rarely cosmetic: take the peninsula out, put a real island in, and turn the room toward the water.

A real kitchen touches plumbing, electrical, mechanical and often structure, which means a building permit and trade permits from the City of Hollywood, plus inspections along the way by inspectors certified through the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals. Purely interior work does not go to Harbor Islands architectural review, but the association still wants your contractor's insurance certificate and gate clearance before the first delivery truck arrives. If a window over the sink grows, that becomes an exterior change, an HVHZ product approval, and an association submittal.

The order of operations is what keeps a kitchen honest. Cabinets are ordered early because good boxes take months, stone is templated after cabinets are set rather than off a drawing, and appliances are confirmed by model number before a single cabinet is cut. Dust walls go up at the kitchen line so the rest of your house stays the finished house. The scope is fixed in writing, a supervisor is here daily, and PGX carries Lic. CGC1539072 with insurance the association can verify.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: Parts of a Harbor Islands kitchen

scope_items.name: Cabinetry built to size
scope_items.desc: Cabinet runs drawn for this house, finished to survive coastal humidity, and taken up to the ceiling where the old soffit used to sit.

scope_items.name: Lighting worth the room
scope_items.desc: Layered ceiling, cabinet and island lighting on the right circuits, plus panel capacity checked before an induction range and a wine wall arrive.

faqs.q: Does a kitchen remodel here need a city permit?
faqs.a: Yes, for anything past new paint and knobs. Moving plumbing, adding circuits, changing ventilation or opening a wall all require permits from the City of Hollywood, and each gets inspected before it is covered. The application itself is the countywide Broward form. Unpermitted kitchen work is one of the first things a buyer's inspector finds, and fixing it later costs more than doing it once.

faqs.q: Does the Harbor Islands association have to approve my kitchen?
faqs.a: For an interior kitchen, generally no. Architectural review exists for what the neighbors can see: elevations, colors, windows, roofs, hardscape. What the association does care about is process. Expect to register the contractor at the gate, provide a certificate of insurance, respect the posted work hours, and keep dumpsters and material staging where they were agreed. We handle that paperwork before the first crew arrives.

faqs.q: How long is my kitchen out of service?
faqs.a: Plan on a couple of months of on-site work for a full kitchen, longer if a structural opening or a relocated wet wall is involved. The bigger clock is fabrication: custom cabinetry commonly runs several months from approved drawings, and stone follows the cabinets. We order long-lead items first and demolish only when the pieces are in hand, so your house is not sitting open waiting.

faqs.q: Can I have a gas range in a Harbor Islands kitchen?
faqs.a: Sometimes, and it needs deciding early rather than at rough-in. If natural gas is not available to the house, the alternative is propane, and that means a tank location, fire code clearances, a permit and a conversation with the association about where the thing sits. Plenty of clients here choose induction instead and never look back. Either way, the appliance package is locked before cabinets are ordered.

faqs.q: What does a kitchen at this level run in Harbor Islands?
faqs.a: Cabinetry, stone and appliances set the tone, and they can differ by a factor of three depending on selections, so a per-foot number is meaningless. We walk the room, write a specification, and quote that. As a high-end contractor we are not competing to be the cheapest bid in Harbor Islands; we compete on the finished room and on a price that holds through the project.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodeling in Harbor Islands FL | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Second-floor baths in Harbor Islands, Hollywood FL rebuilt over tested membranes so nothing reaches the room below. PGX, (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.h1: The bath your builder didn't build
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers, freestanding tubs and stone for Harbor Islands homes, with waterproofing flood-tested before tile. Fully permitted through the City of Hollywood, inspected, and supervised daily by a licensed contractor.
intro_paragraphs: The primary bath in a Harbor Islands house follows a script written around 1999: a corner tub with jets nobody has run in a decade, a glass block window, cultured marble tops, and a shower with a curb, a builder door and one sad niche. Owners in The Estates, Edgewater and Harborside are rewriting it into something calmer — a wet zone with a freestanding tub and a frameless walk-in shower, one long stone vanity, and a closet that finally makes sense with the bedroom next door.

Bathroom work here needs permits from the City of Hollywood Development Services Department, and the inspection sequence is the point rather than the obstacle: plumbing rough, electrical, and the shower pan flood test all get looked at before tile hides them. Broward's code amendments, administered by the Board of Rules and Appeals, govern the details, and any new or enlarged exterior window brings an HVHZ product approval and an association submittal. Nothing about an interior bath goes to architectural review, but everything about it goes past an inspector.

Most of these baths sit on the second floor, directly above a family room ceiling, which is why we treat waterproofing as structure rather than finish. Membranes are installed to the manufacturer's detail and flood-tested, slopes are verified with a level, blocking goes in before the heavy glass is ordered, and the exhaust actually reaches the outside. Scope is fixed in writing, one supervisor runs the job, and PGX has delivered more than 150 permitted and inspected remodels and additions across South Florida.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: How we rebuild a second-floor bath
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Every fixture, slab and membrane is named in the scope before demolition begins. These are the elements Harbor Islands owners ask for most.

scope_items.name: Ventilation and light

faqs.q: Do bathroom remodels need permits in Hollywood?
faqs.a: Anything beyond swapping a vanity top or repainting does. Relocating a drain, adding circuits, changing ventilation or building a new shower requires permits and inspections through the City of Hollywood, on the same countywide Broward application. That inspection record is worth having: it is proof the waterproofing and rough plumbing were verified, which matters when the house eventually sells.

faqs.q: Can we do a curbless shower on the second floor?
faqs.a: Often yes, but it depends on how your second floor was built. Where the upper floor is framed, the structure can usually be dropped or modified to sink the pan; where it is a poured or precast concrete deck, the options narrow and the drain routing decides. On the ground floor, over a slab, it comes down to the waste line and how much concrete we can responsibly cut. We check the drawings and tell you which house you own before you commit.

faqs.q: How disruptive is this to the rest of the house?
faqs.a: Contained, if the contractor bothers. We seal the work zone, run a protected path from the door to the stair, cover finished floors and rails, and clean at the end of each day because in this community the neighbors are ten feet away. Water is shut down only for scheduled windows. Most families stay put, using a secondary bath, for the whole project.

faqs.q: How long does a primary bath take?
faqs.a: Six to twelve weeks of construction is a fair frame for a full primary bath, and it moves with selections. Stone slabs, custom vanities and specialty glass carry lead times that dwarf the labor, so we finalize choices before demolition rather than during it. Waiting on a tile decision with the room already open is how projects quietly double in length.

faqs.q: What does a bathroom at this level cost in Harbor Islands?
faqs.a: It ranges widely, because a guest bath refresh and a full primary suite with a stone wet room are not the same project. Slab selection, plumbing brand, glass and how far the plumbing moves are the real drivers. We would rather scope precisely than throw out a range you cannot rely on. Expect a high-end number, and expect it to be a fixed one.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Tell us what fails you every morning. We come look, measure, and put a real scope and a real number to it, in English o en español.

home-additions.h1: More house on a tight lot
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second-story additions, garage conversions and in-law suites for Harbor Islands homes. Engineered, zoned, taken through association review, permitted by the City of Hollywood, and built under daily supervision.
home-additions.local_heading: Growing a house inside the gates
intro_paragraphs: Lot lines are the first conversation in Harbor Islands. Apart from the estate parcels, most homesites here are compact and tightly platted around canals, cul-de-sacs and the water off Harbor Island Drive, with side setbacks that leave less room than owners expect. That geometry pushes additions upward and backward: a second story over the garage in Harborview, a rear family room and covered terrace in Grand Harbor Estates, a ground-floor in-law suite where a formal dining room has been sitting empty since 2004.

Three separate approvals stack up on an addition here. The City of Hollywood reviews zoning first, since setbacks, lot coverage and height on these plats leave less room than owners expect, then the Building Division reviews the structural drawings under the Florida Building Code as administered in Broward by the Board of Rules and Appeals. Harbor Islands architectural review looks at massing, roof pitch, tile and color so the new volume reads as original. On waterfront lots, the federal fifty-percent substantial improvement rule the city administers through its flood ordinance can shape the budget, so we test it before drawings.

A contractor's experience on an addition is visible from the street. Tying new footings to a twenty-five-year-old foundation, matching stucco texture and barrel tile so the seam disappears, keeping the occupied half of the house dry and livable while the other half is open to the sky: none of that is improvised well. PGX runs one team from feasibility through final inspection, with a fixed written scope, daily supervision, and 20-plus years of building in South Florida behind the schedule we hand you.

scope_items.desc: Family rooms and primary suites pushed toward the water or the lake, with foundations, tie-beams and roof tie-ins engineered as one permitted package.

scope_items.name: Footings, steel and tie-beams
scope_items.desc: The invisible half of the budget: new footings, underpinning where needed, steel and upgraded tie-beams sized for High-Velocity Hurricane Zone wind loads.

faqs.q: Will my lot even allow an addition in Harbor Islands?
faqs.a: That is the first thing we check, and the answer comes from two places. The City of Hollywood's zoning rules for the plat govern setbacks, height and how much of the lot may be covered, and the association's architectural guidelines add their own limits. On these compact homesites the two together often steer a project up rather than out. We run those numbers before anyone pays for a design.

faqs.q: Does the association really review the design?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is not a formality. Harbor Islands was master-planned to look coherent from the street, so architectural review considers massing, roof pitch and tile, stucco texture, window profiles and paint. A design drawn to match the house tends to move; a design that ignores the neighborhood invites revision rounds. We draw for that review from the first sketch instead of arguing with it later.

faqs.q: What is the fifty-percent rule and does it apply to me?
faqs.a: It is the federal substantial improvement standard the city administers through its flood damage prevention ordinance. If the cost of improvement reaches half the market value of the structure, the whole building has to be brought into current flood compliance. On waterfront lots that changes the math, and it is far better understood during feasibility than discovered at permit review. We test it early and tell you plainly.

faqs.q: How long does an addition take from first call to move-in?
faqs.a: Budget real time up front. Design and structural engineering commonly run two to four months, architectural review and city permitting add more, and construction on a substantial addition runs several months beyond that. A year from first conversation to furniture is a realistic frame. We put every phase in writing so nobody is left guessing where the project actually stands.

faqs.q: Is adding on better than buying a bigger house nearby?
faqs.a: Often, if you like your street, your dock and your gate. You keep the location and the water access and buy only the space you were missing, which in this community usually beats climbing the waterfront ladder. It is still major construction with two approval tracks and months of work, so it suits owners planning to stay. We give a candid feasibility read before anything else.

home-additions.cta_sub: Send the survey if you have one. We will talk setbacks, association review and honest numbers before you spend on drawings, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.title: Outdoor Living in Harbor Islands, FL | PGX Builders
outdoor-living.meta_description: Terraces, summer kitchens, seawalls and exteriors in Harbor Islands, Hollywood FL. City and Broward County permits handled. Call PGX at (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Covered terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas, driveways, stucco and impact openings for Harbor Islands homes, with re-roof coordination and seawall or dock work permitted through the city and Broward County.
intro_paragraphs: A Harbor Islands backyard usually starts with what the builder left: a screened cage over a rectangular pool, a field of pavers going grey, and a lot line that ends at a seawall with a private dock beyond it. Homes on Windjammer Way, Mariner Way and Harbor Court look straight across the Intracoastal, and the boats behind them run to Port Everglades to the north or Haulover to the south without a fixed bridge in the way. The upgrade owners want is a genuine outdoor room: covered, lit, plumbed, and pointed at the water.

Exterior work draws the widest set of approvals in this community. The City of Hollywood permits the structures, and Harbor Islands architectural review sees anything visible, from pergola profiles to paint color and driveway material. Seawall and dock work adds Broward County: its Environmental Engineering and Permitting Division licenses work in, on or under surface waters through the Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program, and the county's regional resilience standard sets a minimum crest elevation for new and substantially rehabilitated tidal flood barriers. Re-roofs and new openings need HVHZ product approvals and a secondary water barrier.

Outdoor work gets built to indoor standards or it does not last here. Utilities for a summer kitchen are permitted and inspected like any other gas, water and electrical run. Pergola and trellis footings are engineered for High-Velocity Hurricane Zone uplift rather than sized by eye. Hardware, fasteners and cabinetry are specified for salt air a hundred feet from open water. Add a fixed written scope, daily supervision, tidy staging on narrow streets, and a licensed, insured builder the association can verify.

scope_items.desc: Roofed terraces and shade structures anchored on poured footings, with uplift connections drawn to match the roof pitch already on the house.

scope_items.desc: Permitted water, drain, electrical and fuel runs, marine-grade stainless and weather-rated cabinetry, because outdoor cabinets bought on price corrode within a few seasons here.

scope_items.desc: Replacing tired pavers and slabs with stone or finished concrete, graded so a summer downpour runs away from the house instead of toward it.

scope_items.name: Seawalls, docks and lifts
scope_items.desc: Marine work coordinated through the city and Broward County environmental licensing, with elevation requirements checked before design rather than after a rejection.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint and roof
scope_items.desc: Exterior restoration, color changes taken through architectural review, and re-roof scheduling arranged so new impact openings and tile happen in the right order.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a summer kitchen or pergola here?
faqs.a: Yes on both. The structure needs a building permit from the City of Hollywood, the water, drain, electrical and fuel runs need their own trade permits, and anything visible goes to Harbor Islands architectural review first. Unpermitted patio structures are also the ones that leave during a hurricane, which is a more expensive lesson than the permit was. We manage all of it as part of the job.

faqs.q: Can you rebuild or raise my seawall?
faqs.a: Seawall and dock work is its own permitting track. Beyond the city permit, Broward County licenses work in, on and under surface waters through its Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program, and the county's regional resilience standard governs how high a new or substantially rehabilitated barrier has to sit, stepping minimum elevations up over the coming decades. We start with an assessment and a surveyed elevation, then design to the standard rather than around it.

faqs.q: Will salt air destroy an outdoor kitchen on the Intracoastal?
faqs.a: It will destroy the wrong one quickly. This close to open water we specify marine-grade stainless, powder-coated or naturally inert metals, dense sealed stone, and fasteners chosen for coastal exposure. Big-box outdoor cabinets and bargain hardware rust into a maintenance project within a couple of seasons. Specified correctly the first time, a terrace here ages at roughly the same rate as the house.

faqs.q: Does the association control what my backyard looks like?
faqs.a: For anything the neighbors or the water can see, yes. Architectural review covers structures, roof and paint colors, hardscape materials and often screen enclosures, and it also sets the practical rules: work hours, gate registration, where a dumpster may sit and how deliveries reach a narrow cul-de-sac. We submit for approval and schedule around those rules rather than apologizing for them later.

faqs.q: What does a full backyard rebuild run in Harbor Islands?
faqs.a: Roofed structure, utilities and any marine work drive the number far more than deck area does. A refreshed paver deck is one conversation; a covered outdoor room with a full summer kitchen, drainage, lighting and a rebuilt seawall is a different one entirely. Selections move it as much as size does. After a site walk you get a written specification and a fixed price, not a per-foot guess.

outdoor-living.cta_sub: Bring the dock, the deck and the wish list. You will get a fixed scope and a straight answer, in English o en español.

permitting-compliance.local_heading: A gated street is not an exemption
intro_paragraphs: Harbor Islands is young enough that its first owners are only now selling, refinancing or borrowing against houses they helped build. That is usually when somebody finally reads the file. A title search on Windjammer Way turns up an impact glass permit from years back that never got its final inspection. A lift went in off a dock in Grand Harbor Estates during a quiet season. A generator, a pool heater, a bar sink: none of it difficult behind a guard gate, all of it permanent on paper. The rest are owners with nothing wrong yet, who want the next project on the record from day one.

The permit itself is a City of Hollywood matter. The Building Division inside the Development Services Department reviews the drawings, issues the permit and sends the inspector, on the countywide Broward application every city here files. Behind the city sits another layer: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals administers the Florida Building Code across the county, publishes its amendments, certifies the officials and inspectors who will handle your job, hears appeals and issues formal interpretations when a code section is disputed. Broward is entirely High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so glass, doors and roofing carry HVHZ product approvals into the submittal.

PGX Builders Group is the contractor of record on the application, Lic. CGC1539072, so the license and the liability sit with us rather than with a homeowner signing as owner-builder. Where a submittal needs an architect, an engineer or a surveyor, we retain and coordinate them; we do not pretend to be them. Plan review comments get answered completely the first time, and a supervisor meets every inspector at the door. Twenty-plus years in South Florida, more than 150 remodels and additions, all of them permitted and inspected. In a community this quiet, a clean file is part of the discretion.

scope_items.name: Seawalls, docks and flood rules

faqs.q: Title found an open permit and we close next month. Can it be cleared in time?
faqs.a: Frequently, and the useful clock starts when you call rather than when the lender does. We pull the address file at the City of Hollywood, read what each open record is actually missing, and sort it. Some need only the final inspection nobody ever called. Others need a revision or a letter from an engineer. Work done with no permit at all may need one after the fact, with construction opened up where an inspector can see it. Plan in weeks, not days.

faqs.q: Do I file with the City of Hollywood or with Broward County?
faqs.a: With the city. Hollywood's Building Division, inside Development Services, reviews the plans, issues the permit and sends the inspectors, on the same application form every municipality in Broward uses. The county's role is real but different: the Board of Rules and Appeals administers the code countywide, certifies the officials and inspectors, hears appeals and settles disputed code language, and nothing is filed there. Work in or over the Intracoastal is the exception, adding county environmental licensing on its own track.

faqs.q: The dock, the lift and the window swap were all done before we bought. Now what?
faqs.a: They get legalized, which is more work than permitting them on time and considerably less than the credit a buyer asks for at the table. We document what exists, bring in the engineer or surveyor who can certify what is certifiable, and apply to the city against the code in force today. Replacement glass has to match an approval valid in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so undocumented windows sometimes have to be re-approved or replaced. In-water work adds county environmental review.

faqs.q: The association approved the work. Isn't that the approval that matters here?
faqs.a: It matters, and it is not a permit. Harbor Islands architectural review governs what the community sees: massing, roof, color, hardscape, anything visible from the street or the water. The city governs whether the work is legal, and that is the record a title search, a lender and a buyer's inspector will read years from now. Gate registration and a certificate of insurance are a third thing again. We handle all three in the order that keeps a job moving.

faqs.q: Does building recertification or the milestone inspection apply to my house?
faqs.a: Not to a detached house here. Broward runs a Building Safety Inspection Program through the Board of Rules and Appeals, and one and two family homes are exempt from it, which covers everything behind this gate. Florida's milestone inspection and structural integrity reserve study rules reach condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories or more, so they belong to associations and building owners rather than to you. Where such a report exists, the concrete, railing and waterproofing repairs it calls for are ordinary permitted work we take on.

permitting-compliance.cta_heading: Pull the file before they do
permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Give us the address and the lender's deadline. We read the permit history and hand you a written plan for what it will take, in English o en español.
